positions.summary_short: Crombie pledges to scrap the $2.5-billion downtown redevelopment, hold tax increases at or below inflation, and create an independent Auditor General.
summary_bullets: Pledges to scrap Carolyn Parrish's proposed $2.5-billion downtown redevelopment (Living Arts Centre/civic lands: hotel, convention centre, elevated park), preserving the Living Arts Centre's community and cultural role.
Review the budget line by line, establish an independent Auditor General, and work to keep City tax increases at or below inflation while protecting frontline services.
Bring forward an early-payment property tax discount (rate set through a public financial review); increase the annual property tax rebate to $1,000 for eligible low-income seniors.
Increases annual recreation assistance to $500 per eligible participant; strengthens partnerships to prevent evictions, support food programs and advance affordable rental housing.
positions.verbatim_quote: I will scrap the vanity project and get to work on a future you can afford.
positions.source_title: Crombie Pledges to Scrap Parrish's $2.5-Billion Vanity Project and Put Residents First

positions.summary_short: Crombie would pursue a subway extension into downtown Mississauga, open the Hazel McCallion LRT by end of 2028, and synchronize traffic lights to cut congestion.
summary_bullets: Pursue a Line 2 subway extension into downtown Mississauga and press to open the Hazel McCallion Line by the end of 2028.
Improve bus and GO connections; synchronize traffic lights, fix bottlenecks and coordinate construction so residents get home sooner.
Campaign messaging frames this as 'getting the city moving again' with a subway extension.
positions.verbatim_quote: People are asking for homes they can afford and transit that gets them where they need to go.
positions.source_title: Crombie Pledges to Scrap Parrish's $2.5-Billion Vanity Project and Put Residents First

positions.summary_short: Crombie would return to the Peel Police Services Board and back frontline policing on home invasions, auto theft and extortion.
summary_bullets: Return to the Peel Police Services Board, which incumbent Mayor Parrish quit during the 2025 police-budget fight.
Back frontline police tackling home invasions, auto theft and extortion.
Reduce unnecessary police paperwork so officers spend more time protecting the public.
positions.verbatim_quote: We are in an affordability crisis. This election is about needs, not wants.
positions.source_title: Crombie Pledges to Scrap Parrish's $2.5-Billion Vanity Project and Put Residents First

positions.summary_short: Crombie's platform offers targeted tax deferrals for tariff-hit businesses, 15-day payment for local suppliers, and fast-tracked job-creating investment.
summary_bullets: Provide targeted tax deferrals for tariff-affected businesses.
Pay qualifying local suppliers within 15 days.
'Buy Canadian' procurement and fast-track investments that protect and create Mississauga jobs.
positions.verbatim_quote: We can attract good jobs, build homes and get this city moving.
positions.source_title: Crombie Pledges to Scrap Parrish's $2.5-Billion Vanity Project and Put Residents First

positions.summary_short: Crombie says she wants to get housing built and advance affordable rental housing, redirecting resources from the cancelled redevelopment.
summary_bullets: 'I want to get housing built' — build the downtown loop transit and bring a subway to build a downtown that works for residents.
Redirect resources freed by cancelling the $2.5B redevelopment toward residents' priorities including housing.
Advance affordable rental housing through stronger partnerships and support eviction-prevention programs.
positions.verbatim_quote: I want to get housing built, secure funding to deliver the downtown loop and bring a subway into the heart of Mississauga.
positions.source_title: Crombie Pledges to Scrap Parrish's $2.5-Billion Vanity Project and Put Residents First

positions.summary_short: Parrish says she has already saved taxpayers $45 million via Peel service downloads and is fighting for a fairer police-budget split worth ~$106M more per year.
summary_bullets: Says she has already saved taxpayers $45 million by moving roads ($30M) and waste ($15M) services from Peel Region (heavily subsidized by Mississauga) to the three municipalities.
Publishing an estimated-savings table: e.g. a $1M assessed home would save ~$742.60/year under her full plan.
Next target: a fair Peel police budget split, worth what she estimates at ~$106 million more per year for Mississauga taxpayers.
positions.verbatim_quote: Carolyn Parrish has already saved taxpayers $45 Million.
positions.source_title: Carolyn Parrish For Mayor (campaign homepage)

positions.summary_short: Parrish wants the Peel police cost split moved from 62/38 to 50/50 over three years, asking the province to phase in the change.
summary_bullets: Mississauga taxpayers cover 62% of the Peel Regional Police budget vs Brampton's 38%, despite similar populations; she calls the assessment-based formula unfair since 1974.
Took the funding formula directly to Premier Doug Ford, asking the province to even out the split over a three-year transition so Brampton isn't hit with a sudden tax shock.
Frames the fight as about splitting the bill fairly, not the size of the police budget; notes her late father, Constable Edward Janozeski, served 37 years with Toronto Police.
positions.verbatim_quote: If we can get a fair balance and do it over a three-year period, I think it will work just fine.
positions.source_title: Carolyn Parrish For Mayor (campaign homepage)

positions.summary_short: Parrish highlights the School Streets pilot creating car-free, walkable space around a school at pickup time.
summary_bullets: Backs the School Streets pilot at Sts. Peter & Paul Catholic Elementary School: a car-free street during afternoon pickup, creating safe, community-friendly space for walking and cycling to and from school.
Also championed the decade-long push (since 2017) for the full-size Avro Arrow replica installed at Paul Coffey Park in Malton.
positions.verbatim_quote: Creating safe, community-friendly space for walking and cycling to and from school.
positions.source_title: For One Hour, Kids Owned the Street (campaign story)

positions.summary_short: Damerla would freeze the city-controlled share of property taxes for 2027, cap future increases at inflation, and create an independent Auditor General.
summary_bullets: Freeze the City-controlled share of residential property taxes for 2027 (excluding Region-to-City transfers of roads/waste, offset by lower regional taxes), with no cuts to City services.
From 2028, hold city-controlled increases to inflation unless residents get demonstrable service improvements.
Create an independent Auditor General to investigate waste and report directly to the public, plus a confidential Fraud and Waste Hotline; cites Toronto's AG finding ~$342M in savings 2021-2025.
End severance payments when elected officials voluntarily resign, retire, don't seek re-election, or resign to run for another office.
positions.verbatim_quote: Before City Hall asks residents for more, it needs to look harder for savings, eliminate waste and make every tax dollar work harder.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla proposes a One Mississauga Dashboard to publicly track services, projects and 311 requests, plus a whistleblower-safe fraud hotline under an Auditor General.
summary_bullets: Create the 'One Mississauga Dashboard': one public hub to track city services, projects, budgets, 311 requests and performance.
Connect phone and online 311 systems so a reference number works regardless of how a resident first contacted the City.
Independent Auditor General would publicly report results of waste/fraud investigations while protecting whistleblowers; good-faith reporters protected, not punished.
positions.verbatim_quote: City Hall should make it easy for you to see what you're paying for and whether it's being delivered.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla wants an independent review of the Peel police funding formula, targeted intersection CCTV, a mental-health crisis task force, and justice-system advocacy.
summary_bullets: Demand an independent review of the Peel Police funding formula (Mississauga pays ~62%, ~$93.7M more than a population-based share in 2025, projected $104M in 2026); push a population/service-demand-based formula with provincial help for the transition.
Work with Peel Police on targeted CCTV at major road intersections for investigations — strictly a policing tool, no automated traffic tickets, with privacy rules.
Three-pillar crime plan: modern policing + technology, justice-system reform advocacy (faster trials, stronger action on repeat offenders, bail reform), and value-for-money audits of police spending.
Establish a Mayor's Task Force to improve mental-health crisis response, building on Mobile Crisis Rapid Response Teams (CMHA crisis worker + specially trained officer).
Push the Province for a practical e-bike/e-scooter licensing and registration framework to make enforcement possible.
positions.verbatim_quote: Target crime. Protect privacy. Keep residents safe.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla's OFF We GO transit plan focuses on reliability, 15-minute service and express buses, plus a four-day pothole repair guarantee and keeping existing car lanes.
summary_bullets: 'OFF We GO' transit plan: On Time (transit-priority signalling, better MiWay/GO coordination), Frequent (more 15-minute MiWay service, all-day two-way GO on the Milton Line), Fast (express buses, queue-jump lanes, GO feeder pilots).

Fast Track higher-order transit: Derry, Eglinton and Dixie corridors; fight to bring the subway into Mississauga if extended to Sherway Gardens; push earlier electrification of the Lakeshore GO line as a 'surface subway' with two extra stops.
Extend MiWay's transfer window from 2 to 3 hours in 2028; push the Province to assume Hazel McCallion LRT operating costs; hold Metrolinx accountable for construction delays.
Maintain existing car lanes on busy roads; add bike lanes only where safe, useful and connected, without removing car lanes; use technology and traffic management.
Four-Day Pothole Guarantee for major city roads, with public tracking through the One Mississauga Dashboard.
positions.verbatim_quote: People will choose transit when it is On Time, Frequent and Fast.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla proposes a Clean Parks Guarantee with six times more seasonal by-law officers and published cleanup performance.
summary_bullets: Introduce a 'Clean Parks Guarantee': increase proactive seasonal by-law officers from 4 to 24 in summer, focused on known problem parks.
More frequent scheduled garbage collection at litter hotspots; administrative penalties for littering/illegal dumping where legally available.
Hold large park users/permit holders accountable; publish park issues and cleanup performance on the One Mississauga Dashboard.
positions.verbatim_quote: Clean parks aren't a luxury. They're a basic service in a city that works.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla would speed small-home permitting, expand co-op and non-profit housing, and concentrate intensification near transit with a better mix of housing types.
summary_bullets: Professional Engineer's Seal pilot for small residential projects (garden/laneway suites, small homes, additions) to cut permitting duplication while keeping safety and zoning reviews.
Work with federal/provincial governments to expand co-op and non-profit housing and help first-time buyers; compete aggressively for senior-government housing dollars.
Push a healthier mix: townhomes, semis, family-sized condos, rental housing, smaller senior homes, co-op/non-profit housing.
Concentrate major intensification near transit corridors and growth areas with infrastructure to support it; protect established neighbourhood character; demand complete communities.
positions.verbatim_quote: The goal isn't simply to count how many units we approve. It's to build homes people can actually build their lives in.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Damerla's economic plan centres on tariff-hit business relief, a fast-track lane for manufacturers, a health-innovation hub, and halving small-business permit times.
summary_bullets: Tariff Response Express Lane: faster site-plan/building-permit approvals, one City contact, and an Industrial Retention Team for tariff-hit manufacturers investing or retooling in Mississauga.
Explore property-tax deferrals for qualifying tariff-hit businesses; defer development charges for affected manufacturers expanding/retooling; pay qualifying local suppliers within 15 days.
Use city purchasing power to support Canadian and local businesses; explore Community Improvement Plans tied to real investment and job creation.
First-year Health Innovation & Incubation Hub to commercialize health innovations locally ('Invent it here. Test it here. Fund it here. Build it here.'); Mississauga Global Investment Summit.
Small business: cut average city business-permit processing times by 50%, publish timelines, create a Red Tape Feedback Portal, modernize outdated zoning/parking rules.
positions.verbatim_quote: When a company is ready to invest and protect Mississauga jobs, City Hall needs to move at the speed of business.
positions.source_title: The Platform — What We're Fighting For (Dipika Damerla for Mayor)

positions.summary_short: Tedjo proposes a city housing corporation, tripling missing-middle supply by 2037, six-storey as-of-right on main roads, and a Safe Occupancy rental registry.
summary_bullets: Create a Mississauga Housing Corporation to identify underused municipal and private properties and partner with builders/non-profits so affordable housing is a requirement of new builds.

Goal of tripling the supply of family-oriented missing-middle housing by 2037; expand the Gentle Density Housing Incentive Program to sixplexes; upzone all main roads to allow 6 storeys as-of-right (mixed-use/residential).
Make housing approvals among the fastest in the GTA by resourcing planning staff with expertise and technology.

Replace the lodging-house licensing system with a Safe Occupancy Certificate based on actual safety standards plus a publicly searchable Safe Occupancy Registry, closing a legal gap for renters reporting unsafe conditions.
positions.verbatim_quote: Mississauga needs more homes - but we also need to build the right homes, faster.
positions.source_title: Housing — Alvin Tedjo for Mississauga Mayor

positions.summary_short: Tedjo would freeze the city share of property taxes for two years, permanently freeze-then-defer taxes for qualifying long-time seniors, and credit underspending back to taxpayers.
summary_bullets: Freeze the City of Mississauga's share of residential property tax for two years.

Raise the low-income senior property-tax rebate from $571 to ~$700 (inflation catch-up), renew automatically; after the freeze, qualifying seniors (65+, one home, 20+ years residence) never see another increase — future increases deferred and collected on sale/transfer.
Year-one pause on property-tax interest (up to 3 months); when City Hall underspends, savings return as a credit on the next residential tax bill.

Review/raise the ActiveAssist benefit ($275, unchanged in 10 years); free drop-in swim or skate for kids 12 and under; expand full-day 'Play in the Park' with ~50 student summer jobs; one account showing what residents qualify for; a Seniors' Passport for programs/discounts.
positions.verbatim_quote: Alvin will freeze the City of Mississauga's share of your residential property-tax bill. For two years, that portion of the bill won't go up.
positions.source_title: Affordability — Alvin Tedjo for Mississauga Mayor

positions.summary_short: Tedjo's safety plan focuses on resourcing police, modernizing crime-fighting, and prevention so residents don't accept rising crime as the status quo.
summary_bullets: Cites rising car thefts, home invasions, violent crime and dangerous driving, and higher insurance costs for residents.
Plan: give police the resources they need, modernize how crime is fought, prevent crime before it happens, make every neighbourhood safer.
Bring action and accountability on crime to the Region of Peel.
positions.verbatim_quote: Residents shouldn't have to accept rising crime as the status quo.
positions.source_title: Crime and Safety — Alvin Tedjo for Mississauga Mayor

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz proposes a 5% budget reduction plan, halving council office budgets, and an independent Auditor General shared across Peel cities.
summary_bullets: A '-5% Reduction Budget Plan' for Mississauga: full costed review of every City service and corporate account; corporate overhead (administration, consultants, travel) examined before front-line services.

Council cuts its own budget first: halve the Mayor's and every Councillor's discretionary office budget, end year-to-year carryover of unspent money, ban elected officials giving public money as personal donations.
Hire an independent Auditor General; publish budgets, contracts, expenses and FOI answers by default; share watchdogs across Peel cities so no single mayor can fire them.

Argues 'free' services still cost taxpayers (e.g. free senior transit ~$1.7M/yr in forgone fares); demands published cost and payer before any service is stamped 'free'; warns tax freezes without plans mean bigger hikes or hidden cuts later.
positions.verbatim_quote: I can read a police or municipal budget like a McDonald's menu: I know where the beef is and where the fat is hiding. I can judge the operational value of a police budget!
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz for Mayor — Get_Ready_Ontario (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz would create a civilian Community Response Unit for non-crime 911 calls so police focus on real crime, without cutting police funding.
summary_bullets: Community Response Unit (CRU): 305 trained civilian responders to handle ~4-in-10 911 calls that aren't crimes (wellness, mental health, noise, minor crashes), freeing police for real crime.
Removes no officers or dollars from the police budget; costs ~$27.4M/year (~$38/resident); designed to qualify for existing federal/provincial grants.
Notes Peel Regional Police's budget plan growing toward $1.2B by 2029, and questions what each candidate's real plan is to control those costs without weakening neighbourhood safety.
Points to his own record: 'the only candidate who has actually planned and executed large scale front line police operations' in Canada's largest city police service.
positions.verbatim_quote: Let our officers focus on crime. Give the calls that were never police work to trained civilian staff instead.
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz for Mayor — Get_Ready_Ontario (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz says data centres belong outside city limits, citing non-stop noise, health impacts and property values.
summary_bullets: 'Data centres belong outside city limits!' — calls them power and water plants, not warehouses.
Cites non-stop noise affecting residents' health, daily lives and property values.
Questions why city council still can't say NO: 'Money (tax revenue) or your community? Which did the city choose?'
positions.verbatim_quote: Data centres are power and water plants, not warehouses.
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz for Mayor — Get_Ready_Ontario (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz advocates a 2-cent-per-litre gas levy to fund transit, pitched to the province rather than as a new property tax.
summary_bullets: Proposes a small 2-cent/litre gas levy for transit: ~$8M for the city, ~$16M for Peel; notes it works in Victoria and Montreal.
Frames it as advocacy to Queen's Park, not a unilateral promise, and as a dedicated transit funding tool that adds no new property tax.
positions.verbatim_quote: City has no transit funding tool of its own.
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz for Mayor — Get_Ready_Ontario (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz proposes a 1,000-job Youth Corps, full funding for women's shelters, and a community land trust for permanently affordable housing.
summary_bullets: Mississauga Youth Corps: ~1,000 paid 12-month jobs a year for ages 18-21, no degree/experience required, city-brokered placements across city departments, colleges and tech firms; paid by federal/provincial grants at zero cost to taxpayers (~$27.5M in wages, ~$40M in local activity).
Food security: 503,705 food bank visits last year (~1 in 3 a child); city land, waived fees and matched donations to help locals win existing federal/provincial money.
A safe bed for every woman fleeing violence: fund shelters like fire and ambulance — in full; press the province to declare intimate partner violence an epidemic.
Community Land Trust for permanently affordable homes: city gives surplus land instead of selling it; rent tied to income (~30% of earnings) for those who can never afford market rent.
positions.verbatim_quote: Every dollar of wages is paid by the federal and provincial governments, not by Mississauga taxpayers.
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz for Mayor — Get_Ready_Ontario (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Matulewicz says his priority is recovering Mississauga's $500-million share of the provincial funding shortfall, plus homelessness, affordability and public safety.
summary_bullets: Wants to make back the $500-million shortfall the City of Mississauga faces due to the gap in provincial funding (Peel residents get $578 less per resident annually in provincial funding than the Ontario average; cumulative shortfall $868M/year).
Campaign priorities: improve emergency services, affordability, homelessness, public safety and housing; informed by his years in the Toronto police department.
On homelessness: 'You never forget when you have to go into a cardboard box, or a tent or a blanket,' he said of being assigned to oversee family disputes and the homeless.
positions.verbatim_quote: Homelessness is not a crime—and it's cheaper to house a person than to police them.
positions.source_title: Mike Matulewicz's grassroots campaign to be Mississauga mayor highlights many big issues facing his city (The Pointer)
